title: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 — Section 20
act: The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005

legal_context.subject: Monetary reliefs arising from domestic violence
legal_context.chapter: Chapter IV — Procedure for obtaining orders of reliefs
legal_context.important_note: Section 20 allows the Magistrate to direct monetary relief to meet expenses incurred and losses suffered by the aggrieved person and any child as a result of domestic violence.

section_20.title: Monetary reliefs

subsection_1.intro: While disposing of an application under sub-section (1) of section 12, the Magistrate may direct the respondent to pay monetary relief to meet the expenses incurred and losses suffered by the aggrieved person and any child of the aggrieved person as a result of the domestic violence.

included_reliefs.c: Loss caused due to the destruction, damage or removal of any property from the control of the aggrieved person.
included_reliefs.d: Maintenance for the aggrieved person as well as her children, if any, including an order under or in addition to an order of maintenance under section 125 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 or any other law for the time being in force.

statutory_text.subsection_2: The monetary relief granted under this section shall be adequate, fair and reasonable and consistent with the standard of living to which the aggrieved person is accustomed.
statutory_text.subsection_3: The Magistrate shall have the power to order an appropriate lump sum payment or monthly payments of maintenance, as the nature and circumstances of the case may require.
statutory_text.subsection_4: The Magistrate shall send a copy of the order for monetary relief made under sub-section (1) to the parties to the application and to the in charge of the police station within the local limits of whose jurisdiction the respondent resides.
statutory_text.subsection_5: The respondent shall pay the monetary relief granted to the aggrieved person within the period specified in the order under sub-section (1).
statutory_text.subsection_6: Upon failure by the respondent to make payment in terms of the order under sub-section (1), the Magistrate may direct the employer or a debtor of the respondent to directly pay to the aggrieved person or deposit with the court a portion of the wages, salaries or debt due to or accrued to the credit of the respondent, which amount may be adjusted towards the monetary relief payable.

section_20.plain_summary: Section 20 provides a statutory route for monetary relief where domestic violence has resulted in expenses or losses. The relief may include loss of earnings, medical expenses, property-related losses, and maintenance for the aggrieved person and her children.
key_elements: The provision operates in connection with an application under section 12.
The Magistrate may direct the respondent to pay monetary relief.
Relief may address expenses incurred and losses suffered as a result of domestic violence.
Loss of earnings may be included.
Loss caused by destruction, damage or removal of property may be included.
Maintenance for the aggrieved person and her children may be included.
Maintenance under or in addition to maintenance under another law may be covered.
Monetary relief should be adequate, fair and reasonable.
The relief should be consistent with the standard of living to which the aggrieved person is accustomed.
Maintenance may be ordered as a lump sum or through monthly payments.
The section also provides a mechanism concerning non-payment of ordered monetary relief.

application_to_alimony_plus.calculator_rule: Section 20 does not provide a fixed mathematical formula or guaranteed percentage for calculating monetary relief or maintenance.
application_to_alimony_plus.safety_rule: The AI should explain the statutory categories and conditions without deciding whether a user is legally entitled to relief or predicting a court's order.
application_to_alimony_plus.human_review: Fact-specific questions involving domestic violence, eligibility, overlapping maintenance proceedings, evidence, or interpretation of the Act should be escalated for appropriate legal or human review.
